'''Te Tai Tokerau Party''' is a [[List of political parties in New Zealand|political party in New Zealand]]. Founded in 2026 by [[Te Tai Tokerau]] MP [[Mariameno Kapa-Kingi]], it is standing two candidates in the [[2026 New Zealand general election]]. Kapa-Kingi was elected with [[Te Pāti Māori]] in [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023]], but was suspended and expelled in 2025, in actions that were subsequently overturned by the [[High Court of New Zealand|High Court]].
==Background==
[[Mariameno Kapa-Kingi]] was elected to the [[New Zealand Parliament]] representing [[Te Tai Tokerau]] in 2023, as a member of [[Te Pāti Māori]]. Following tensions between Kapa-Kingi and the leadership of Te Pāti Māori, she was suspended from the party in October 2025, and expelled by a vote of Te Pāti Māori's National Council in the weeks after.<ref name="Dunlop-2026">{{cite news |last1=Dunlop |first1=Māni |title=High Court rules Mariameno Kapa-Kingi expulsion from Te Pāti Māori unlawful |url=https://www.teaonews.co.nz/2026/03/10/high-court-rules-mariameno-kapa-kingi-expulsion-from-te-pati-maori-unlawful-reinstated/ |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[Te Ao Māori News]] |date=10 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918224348/https://www.teaonews.co.nz/2026/03/10/high-court-rules-mariameno-kapa-kingi-expulsion-from-te-pati-maori-unlawful-reinstated/ |archive-date=18 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> The [[High Court of New Zealand|High Court]] ruled in March 2026 that Kapa-Kingi's suspension and expulsion was unlawful. Justice Paul Radich found that the proceedings did not comply with the party's [[Wiktionary:kawa#Noun_14|kawa]], and that the [[Tikanga Māori|tikanga]] principles required by Te Pāti Māori's constitution were not upheld.<ref name="Dunlop-2026" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Hanly |first1=Lillian |title=Mariameno Kapa-Kingi officially reinstated to Te Pāti Māori |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/589156/mariameno-kapa-kingi-officially-reinstated-to-te-pati-maori |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=10 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918224506/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/589156/mariameno-kapa-kingi-officially-reinstated-to-te-pati-maori |archive-date=18 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Kapa-Kingi described the ruling as "justice [for] Te Tai Tokerau voters", and said that she would seek to stand again for Te Tai Tokerau at the [[2026 New Zealand general election|2026 election]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hanly |first1=Lillian |title=Court ruling 'brought justice to Te Tai Tokerau voters', Te Pāti Māori MP Mariameno Kapa-Kingi says |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/589202/court-ruling-brought-justice-to-te-tai-tokerau-voters-te-pati-maori-mp-mariameno-kapa-kingi-says |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=11 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918224613/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/589202/court-ruling-brought-justice-to-te-tai-tokerau-voters-te-pati-maori-mp-mariameno-kapa-kingi-says |archive-date=18 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Dexter |first1=Giles |title=Mariameno Kapa-Kingi unsure if future lies with Te Pāti Māori or as independent |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/589385/mariameno-kapa-kingi-unsure-if-future-lies-with-te-pati-maori-or-as-independent |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=12 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918224718/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/589385/mariameno-kapa-kingi-unsure-if-future-lies-with-te-pati-maori-or-as-independent |archive-date=18 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

While Te Pāti Māori accepted the ruling and began voting on Kapa-Kingi's behalf in Parliament, ''[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]'' reported on 8 May 2026 that Kapa-Kingi and Te Pāti Māori were not working together, and that issues Kapa-Kingi had wished to resolve before rejoining Te Pāti Māori remained unresolved.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McConnell |first1=Glenn |title=Te Pāti Māori in crisis, MPs could walk out ahead of election |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360976177/te-pati-maori-crisis-mps-could-walk-out-ahead-election |access-date=19 September 2026 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=8 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919011728/https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360976177/te-pati-maori-crisis-mps-could-walk-out-ahead-election |archive-date=19 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>
==Foundation and 2026 election==
Kapa-Kingi announced the formation of Te Tai Tokerau Party on 11 May 2026.<ref name="Gabel-2026">{{cite news |last1=Gabel |first1=Julia |title=Mariameno Kapa-Kingi leaves Te Pāti Māori, starts new party |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/mariameno-kapa-kingi-leaves-te-pati-maori-starts-new-party/QSLN7FWU3VF6HOOWZFOGALJYEI/ |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=11 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918231955/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/mariameno-kapa-kingi-leaves-te-pati-maori-starts-new-party/QSLN7FWU3VF6HOOWZFOGALJYEI/ |archive-date=18 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Dexter-2026">{{cite news |last1=Dexter |first1=Giles |title=Te Pāti Māori splits as MP Mariameno Kapa-Kingi announces new Te Tai Tokerau Party |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/594843/te-pati-maori-splits-as-mp-mariameno-kapa-kingi-announces-new-te-tai-tokerau-party |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=11 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918231923/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/594843/te-pati-maori-splits-as-mp-mariameno-kapa-kingi-announces-new-te-tai-tokerau-party |archive-date=18 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Kapa-Kingi said she would only return to Te Pāti Māori if party president [[John Tamihere]] stood down, [[Te Tai Tonga]] MP [[Tākuta Ferris]] was returned to the party, and a public apology from the party leadership was given.<ref name="Hu-2026">{{cite news |last1=Hu |first1=Justin |title=Kapa-Kingi splits from Te Pāti Māori, launches new party |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/05/11/kapa-kingi-splits-from-te-pati-maori-launches-new-party/ |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[1News]] |date=11 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918231937/https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/05/11/kapa-kingi-splits-from-te-pati-maori-launches-new-party/ |archive-date=18 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Stuff-2026">{{cite news |title=Rebel MP Mariameno Kapa-Kingi quitting Te Pāti Māori to start own party |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360977114/former-te-pati-maori-mp-kapa-kingi-start-own-political-party |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=11 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918232030/https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360977114/former-te-pati-maori-mp-kapa-kingi-start-own-political-party |archive-date=18 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> She stated that the process of her reinstatement to Te Pāti Māori had not "occurred in any real, substantial way".<ref name="Hu-2026" /> Kapa-Kingi's announcement was reported as a split from Te Pāti Māori.<ref name="Gabel-2026" /><ref name="Dexter-2026" /><ref name="Hu-2026" /><ref name="Stuff-2026" />

Kapa-Kingi cited "[[tino rangatiratanga]], local decision-making and mana mokopuna" as foundational principles of the party.<ref name="Dexter-2026" /><ref name="Hu-2026" /> In an interview with ''The Hui'', Kapa-Kingi described her focus as "whare, [[whenua]] and [[whānau]]",{{efn|This was translated by ''The Hui'' as meaning "housing, land and family".<ref name="Stuff-2026" />}} and said her new party was designed specifically for the electorate of Te Tai Tokerau.<ref name="Stuff-2026" /> In the same interview, she said that she would consider working with the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]] after the 2026 election if party leader [[Christopher Luxon]] sought her support.<ref name="Hu-2026" />

At a media conference the day after, Kapa-Kingi said that near 200 people had joined the party as dues-paying members, with 500 required to be registered.<ref name="Hu-2026a">{{cite news |last1=Hu |first1=Justin |title=Kapa-Kingi talks plan for new party after Te Pāti Māori split |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/05/12/kapa-kingi-talks-plan-for-new-party-after-te-pati-maori-split/ |access-date=19 September 2026 |work=[[1News]] |date=12 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919000535/https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/05/12/kapa-kingi-talks-plan-for-new-party-after-te-pati-maori-split/ |archive-date=19 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Tswanya-2026">{{cite news |last1=Tswanya |first1=Yolisa |title=Mariameno Kapa-Kingi’s Te Tai Tokerau Party aims for long-term change |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/northland-age/news/mariameno-kapa-kingis-te-tai-tokerau-party-aims-for-long-term-change/LC2XHP2ROZFE3JUMUHK6HOLWWM/ |access-date=19 September 2026 |work=[[The Northland Age]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919000618/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/northland-age/news/mariameno-kapa-kingis-te-tai-tokerau-party-aims-for-long-term-change/LC2XHP2ROZFE3JUMUHK6HOLWWM/ |archive-date=19 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> She said that the party had not yet decided whether to run candidates outside of Te Tai Tokerau, although it was being considered, and that she would not rule out working with any party in Parliament.<ref name="Hu-2026a" /> [[Eru Kapa-Kingi]], Mariameno Kapa-Kingi's son, celebrated the party's launch but said he would keep his involvement in politics limited, focusing instead on advocacy and education.<ref name="Tswanya-2026" />

In response to her announcement, Te Pāti Māori wished Kapa-Kingi well but confirmed that they would stand a candidate in all seven Māori electorates at the 2026 election.<ref name="Gabel-2026" /> Later in the month, [[Aperahama Edwards]] was announced as the Te Pāti Māori candidate in Te Tai Tokerau.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Crimp |first1=Lauren |title=Aperahama Edwards to run for Te Pāti Māori in Te Tai Tokerau |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/northland-age/news/mariameno-kapa-kingis-te-tai-tokerau-party-aims-for-long-term-change/LC2XHP2ROZFE3JUMUHK6HOLWWM/ |access-date=19 September 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=27 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919000403/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/596458/aperahama-edwards-to-run-for-te-pati-maori-in-te-tai-tokerau |archive-date=19 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Both [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour]] leader [[Chris Hipkins]] and National minister [[Chris Bishop]] suggested that the name of the new party would fall foul of electoral law, due to it being named for the electorate of Te Tai Tokerau.<ref name="Dexter-2026" /><ref name="Crimp-2026">{{cite news |last1=Crimp |first1=Lauren |title=New Te Tai Tokerau Party may not be able to contest election under that name, Bishop says |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/594951/new-te-tai-tokerau-party-may-not-be-able-to-contest-election-under-that-name-bishop-says |access-date=19 September 2026 |date=12 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919001916/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/594951/new-te-tai-tokerau-party-may-not-be-able-to-contest-election-under-that-name-bishop-says |archive-date=19 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Te Tai Tokerau Party was registered by the [[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] on 5 August.<ref name="Gabel-2026a">{{cite news |last1=Gabel |first1=Julia |title=Election 2026: Mariameno Kapa-Kingi’s new party approved by Electoral Commission |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/election-2026-mariameno-kapa-kingis-new-party-approved-by-electoral-commission/DFSW2HKZVNDQZJPMGELK3NP3AY/ |access-date=19 September 2026 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=5 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919002554/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/election-2026-mariameno-kapa-kingis-new-party-approved-by-electoral-commission/DFSW2HKZVNDQZJPMGELK3NP3AY/ |archive-date=19 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Electoral Commission considered the possibility of the party name confusing or misleading voters, but decided that the chance of this happening was not likely enough to refuse registration.<ref name="Gabel-2026a"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Electoral Commission Board decisions on party registration and logo applications and applications to vary party names and logos |url=https://elections.nz/assets/pagecomponent-file-files/Party-and-logo-registration-decisions-August-2026.pdf |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=19 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919003552/https://elections.nz/assets/pagecomponent-file-files/Party-and-logo-registration-decisions-August-2026.pdf |archive-date=19 September 2026 |page=3 |date=August 2026}}</ref>

The party is standing two candidates at the 2026 election: Kapa-Kingi in Te Tai Tokerau, and [[Kyla Campbell-Kamariera]] as a list-only candidate.<ref name="Dunlop-2026a">{{cite news |last1=Dunlop |first1=Māni |title=Four candidates, one sprawling rohe and a Māori seat that could go anywhere |url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/nz-news/361092598/four-candidates-one-sprawling-rohe-and-maori-seat-could-go-anywhere |access-date=11 October 2026 |work=[[Sunday Star-Times]] |date=11 October 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011061902/https://www.thepost.co.nz/nz-news/361092598/four-candidates-one-sprawling-rohe-and-maori-seat-could-go-anywhere |archive-date=11 October 2026 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="RNZ-2026">{{cite news |title=Former Te Pāti Māori electorate executive member becomes list candidate for Te Tai Tokerau Party |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/1496365/former-te-pati-maori-electorate-executive-member-becomes-list-candidate-for-te-tai-tokerau-party |access-date=11 October 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=21 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011061928/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/1496365/former-te-pati-maori-electorate-executive-member-becomes-list-candidate-for-te-tai-tokerau-party |archive-date=11 October 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |title=Candidate and party lists released |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2026/candidate-and-party-lists-released |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=11 October 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/73ELK |archive-date=11 October 2026 |date=9 October 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Kapa-Kingi is the party's leader.<ref name="RNZ-2026" /><ref name="Tipene-Allan-2026">{{cite news |last1=Tipene-Allan |first1=Rukuwai |title=Tai Tokerau demands constitutional recognition for He Whakaputanga |url=https://www.teaonews.co.nz/2026/10/20/tai-tokerau-demands-constitutional-recognition-for-he-whakaputanga/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=[[Te Ao Māori News]] |date=20 October 2026 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20261021052939/https://www.teaonews.co.nz/2026/10/20/tai-tokerau-demands-constitutional-recognition-for-he-whakaputanga/ |archive-date=21 October 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Campbell-Kamariera is a former student organiser at the [[University of Waikato]], and has previously served as co-chair of Te Pāti Māori's electorate executive in Te Tai Tokerau.<ref name="RNZ-2026" /> Kapa-Kingi is campaigning for both the party vote and the candidate vote in Te Tai Tokerau.<ref name="1News-2026">{{cite news |title=Te Tai Tokerau: Meet the candidates vying for the northern seat |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/10/22/te-tai-tokerau-meet-the-candidates-vying-for-the-northern-seat/ |access-date=22 October 2026 |work=[[1News]] |date=22 October 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261022224144/https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/10/22/te-tai-tokerau-meet-the-candidates-vying-for-the-northern-seat/ |archive-date=22 October 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> She has said that a high enough party vote for her party could see both her and Campbell-Kamariera elected, potentially resulting in four wāhine Māori from Tai Tokerau being elected to parliament.{{efn|The [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green]] and Labour candidates in Te Tai Tokerau, [[Willow-Jean Prime]] and [[Hūhana Lyndon]], both have high list rankings on their respective party lists that could see them elected irregardless of winning the electorate.<ref name="Dunlop-2026a" /><ref name="1News-2026" />}}<ref name="Dunlop-2026a" /><ref name="1News-2026" /> The party has positioned itself as an advocate for Te Tai Tokerau, and for centering mokopuna in decision-making.<ref name="Tipene-Allan-2026"/><ref name="1News-2026" />
